_comment: The next-release lane as a graph the JEV graph guard judges. The strategic decision - which node lands FIRST - is made by JEV from the evidence, not asserted by the seat. Run: python harness/harness2/compositor.py --mode graph --input harness/next-release/graph.json --wave next-release
_evidence: docs/intake/next-release-intake-2026-11-06.md (adjudicated 2026-11-06) and docs/intake/src/synapse_next_release_blueprint.md (SHA-256 167ca678f620e6a0) Revised 2026-11-07: RULING-2026-11-07-round2.md (R1-R4) adds NR-SPARSE-RENDER, two owner-file extensions and behavioural predicates.
objective: Deliver one trustworthy loop: prove which render products this attempt produced, report authored writes truthfully through every installed route, and qualify one useful OpenCV 5.1 CUDA vision chain on the RTX 4090 behind a supervised worker, with durable evidence. Land the evidence and the contract fixes first, then the GPU feasibility, then the integrated slice; qualify the final artifact pair last.
standards: Law 1: every check must be able to fail. A check that cannot fail is deleted rather than kept green.
Law 2: no number without a producer path. Every figure names the command or probe that produces it.
Law 3: status describes what happened, not what was intended.
Probe truth beats pinned constants: where the live build disagrees with a document, the live build wins.
One owner per file. Two nodes that claim the same file are serialized by plain code; a conflict is a finding, not a race.
Absence of a symbol from a table is not proof of absence. The decisive test is calling it on an instance.
No hardcoded user paths. Every probe and the installer must work on a clean machine.
A GPU flag, device count or utilisation percentage is not a CUDA-success receipt. The executed dispatch branch is.
A result file is not success; a committed terminal receipt is. An orphan after a crash is evidence, not a pass.

nodes.title: Make the live render path honour an explicit frame list
nodes.why: NR-PLAN-TRUTH grades the artist's sparse set in the driver, but the shipped handler reads only start_frame/end_frame/step, render_farm builds a contiguous range, and the MCP schema exposes no frames, so a sparse request still renders the invented frame. The seam crosses an ownership boundary (HANDS render handlers vs CONDUCTOR autonomy), so it is its own node rather than an extension.

nodes.title: Make the original render plan immutable and reconcile sparse, missing and unsupported shapes
nodes.why: G101 and G32 prove per-attempt product truth; neither keeps the original plan immutable nor computes retry targets from it. Sparse [1,3] with a retry [3], a missing terminal product with no evaluation row, and a multi-render-step plan that is silently truncated to the first step are all still reachable. The blueprint's adversarial cases in section 12.2 are the fixtures. Round-two ruling R2: models.py joins the node because the report must carry executed state; the predicate is behavioural (R4) after the attack proved the grep could not fail.

nodes.title: Give authored writes a receipt that survives success, failure and every installed route
nodes.why: G25 returns observed, mismatch and a refusal, but a lost transport loses the detail, an uninspectable parm can read as no animation, and queued mutations carry no precondition. The blueprint's section 6 receipt (request, write, readback, recovery, error) and the raw-authored comparison domain are the contract; the legacy observed value stays evaluated. Round-two ruling R3: the contract is every installed route, so the rewrap, stdio server and panel executor join the node; the predicate is behavioural (R4).

nodes.title: Prove one useful OpenCV 5.1 CUDA chain on the RTX 4090 and freeze its build
nodes.why: Nothing in the repo establishes a working OpenCV 5.1 CUDA build on Windows. The official wheels are CPU-only. This node answers the only question that can stop the release: does the named chain execute, with which exact commits, toolchain, module flags and CUDA runtime, and what does it cost. It is a probe plus a build lock, not a product change.

nodes.title: Qualify the GPU chain against analytic fixtures and an independent CPU reference
nodes.why: Source support, a built module, an executed call and a release-qualified operation are four different states. The blueprint's hand-computable fixtures (neutral RGB ramps, the 11x11 census, signed HDR, NaN/Inf counts, equality at the FP32 threshold) and the backend witness are what turn the second state into the fourth.

nodes.title: Freeze one image and evidence contract: named RGB, derived Y, invalid-sample policy
nodes.why: T1 averages channels and the beauty ingest defaults to a subimage, so alpha and data channels can enter luminance. The Y coefficients must come from the declared RGB-to-XYZ transform, not from Rec.709 weights applied to ACEScg. Source-invalid pixels must block dependent statistics with exact counts rather than being dropped or zeroed.

nodes.title: Run the vision chain in a supervised worker through one thin host adapter
nodes.why: RETINA has modules and a designed process boundary, not a deployed executable path. The worker must own its cv2/OIIO/CUDA binaries outside Houdini's DLL search path, take allowlisted operations and read-only roots, and run off the main thread. This is also the first place the evidence envelope crosses a process boundary.

nodes.title: Publish results durably: one terminal receipt, restart-rebuildable, late replies never win
nodes.why: Without a terminal selection receipt, a result file after a crash, a lost acknowledgement or a superseded request can all read as success. The repo already has the atomic publication pattern in loop/coordinator.py; this node applies it to RETINA requests and results, including cancellation ordering and orphan quarantine.

nodes.title: Ship an independently versioned worker artifact and qualify the host/worker pair and rollback
nodes.why: The payload builder ships an allowlist; adding worker sources does not ship them. The release needs a worker build lock, a host/worker compatibility handshake, and a tested data-preserving rollback. Current Setup refuses ordinary downgrades and refuses maintenance while Houdini runs, so rollback is a procedure to qualify, not a flag to flip.

nodes.title: Make the third-party notice set, CUDA EULA compliance and Qt relinkability a release gate
nodes.why: SYNAPSE is MIT and OpenCV/contrib are Apache-2.0, so nothing blocks commercial use. The obligations are concrete: Apache/BSD notices, the NVIDIA Attachment A binaries and EULA text, OPENCV_ENABLE_NONFREE=OFF in the build lock, and the pre-existing PySide6 LGPLv3 relinkability duty. A release that misses them is a legal defect, not a documentation one.

nodes.title: Curated memory handoff and the isolated SL0 pilot, after the core release
nodes.why: The blueprint keeps these explicitly out of the release. They are listed so the graph does not silently drop them, and parked so plain code does not schedule them.
nodes.parked: Follow-on. Neither blocks the core release.

edges.why: there is nothing to qualify until a build and a chain exist
the contract must name operations the qualified build actually dispatches
the worker implements a contract; it does not invent one
a worker that cannot prove its backend has nothing to ship
publication rules are meaningful only once a worker writes results
the pair is qualified against committed receipts, not against ad-hoc files
the product key and attempt identity the envelope carries come from the plan
vision proposals may only mutate through the authored-write receipt path
no artifact pair ships without its notices and EULA compliance
follow-ons start after the release, not beside it
the plan's sparse set is only meaningful once the live path renders exactly those frames

seams.seam: the render plan is the only source of what was asked for
seams.blast_radius: every retry, every coverage denominator, every 'missing' claim

seams.seam: the evidence envelope crosses the process boundary
seams.blast_radius: T0/T1 verdicts, the worker result, the panel readout

seams.seam: the worker owns native binaries outside Houdini's search path
seams.blast_radius: the DCC's image I/O, every render, the panel's import graph

seams.seam: the installer allowlist decides what ships
seams.blast_radius: the worker exists in development and is absent in the release

seams.seam: the GPU profile is persisted state
seams.blast_radius: a silent CPU fallback can satisfy nothing while reporting success
